transcript:
Header: 2027-06-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Noah (Product), Lena (GrandBay Head ML), Marcus (Infra), Priya (CTO)

00:00 Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Aisha from Redwood Inference, Miguel's my SE, Noah product. Quick roll call?
00:07 Lena: Lena here.
00:08 Marcus: Marcus.
00:09 Priya: Priya on for CTO spot.
00:12 Miguel: Awesome, we'll jump straight into the Optimize console demo, focusing on prefetch and batching recs for your chat agent workload that you sent over. Quick note — I might say K V cache or KV cache interchangeably, and prefetch sometimes hyphenated.
00:28 Aisha: Goal for today is practical: show how console's savings sim maps to your traffic mix, recommend a prefetch window and batching/concurrency knobs, and align on a pilot that proves out cost delta without bumping latency beyond your 200ms soft SLO.
00:44 Priya: 200ms is our target 95p, but if cost reduction is large and 99p moves to 250ms that might still be fine depending on outcomes, we need the numbers.
00:55 Miguel: Great, I'll start with the cost-simulator. (screen share) Here's the Optimize console. On the left is model routing, center is prefetch policy, right is the cost breakdown. I'm going to load the 'GrandBay-support-v1' workload you uploaded.
01:12 Miguel: The simulator assumes a mixed session distribution: 60% short sessions (<128 tokens), 30% mid (128-512), 10% long (>512). That's based on the sample you provided, Lena. Is that still representative?
01:24 Lena: Yes that's close; we see a tail of very long context sessions from account managers — those are the latency-sensitive ones.
01:30 Miguel: Perfect. Two levers we demo: 1) prefix/KV lookahead prefetch (we call it lookahead caching in console) and 2) request batching + concurrency limits. Prefetch reduces per-token generation by warming the KV cache so long contexts don't pay full forward cost every time, but prefetching increases background work and memory usage. Batching reduces per-token kernel overhead but can increase tail latency when requests wait to fill batches.
02:02 Marcus: For infra, two practical Qs: Can prefetching run on a separate pool so it doesn't steal capacity from live requests? And what about eviction pressure / memory on our Dedicated pools?
02:12 Miguel: Yes you can pin prefetch to a lower-cost background pool or use burst-capacity. Console's policy lets you route prefetch jobs to a separate node group (we expose that as 'prefetchRoutingPool' in the API). Eviction is TTL-based and size-limited; we surface expected memory per session in the console so you can see when you hit memory thresholds.
02:31 Aisha: We'll show a scenario where prefetch on a warm pool gives 40% token-cost savings for the long-session portion while keeping 95p under 220ms.
02:40 Miguel: (adjusting knobs) First simulation: No prefetch, batching=auto (small batch threshold), concurrency cap=80. Baseline cost estimate: $0.053 per 1k tokens effective for your mix — that's a combined hosting + token compute estimate.
03:00 Lena: That per-1k number seems high compared to our on-prem number, but we haven't added infra ops cost to yours so maybe comparable.
03:10 Miguel: Right, our number is fully managed with SLA. Next, enable lookahead prefetch with a 32-token horizon for sessions flagged as 'long' (console will detect session age and flag after token 256). Also route prefetch to 'warm-background' pool with capped prefetch concurrency 20. Keep batching at auto but increase max batch size to 64 for throughput.
03:40 Miguel: New estimate: effective cost drops to $0.032 per 1k tokens, ~40% saving. 95p latency moves from 190ms to 215ms in the sim for long sessions, and short sessions unchanged.
03:54 Priya: So the left tail is fine, but what happens on sudden spikes — do prefetch jobs bump up longer queues and cause short sessions to see higher latency?
04:06 Miguel: That's why we route prefetch to a separate pool by default in the recommendation. If you can't run separate pools we provide QoS routing — prefetch has lowest priority and system will throttle prefetch if live throughput climbs. Console sim includes a 'spike' toggle, let's flip it on to see a 3x sudden spike.
04:26 Miguel: (flip) Under 3x spike, if prefetch is on the same pool without QoS, short sessions 95p climbs to ~340ms — not acceptable. With separate prefetch pool or strict QoS, short sessions remain ~210ms while prefetch backlog grows and gets trimmed by TTL.
04:42 Marcus: That addresses the concern. We will likely want prefetch on a distinct node pool inside Dedicated; that aligns with our security/tenant isolation.
04:52 Lena: Curious — how brittle is the prefetch window choice? If we pick 32 tokens vs 64, what's the marginal benefit?
05:00 Miguel: Good question. The console provides an incremental delta chart. In your workload the marginal returns diminish after 48 tokens for long sessions because the model KV hit-rate saturates; 32 tokens captured ~85% of the potential savings, 48 tokens ~93%, 64 tokens only ~96% but with memory up 30%. So recommendation: start at 32, move to 48 for VIP accounts where cost matters more.
05:28 Noah: Also note that prefetch has a priming cost — your billing sees background prefetch tokens. In the cost simulator we show net token delta (prefetch tokens minus saved generation tokens). For your case net tokens go down because long sessions avoid very expensive forward passes.
05:42 Priya: What about eviction policy — LRU vs TTL? Marcus prefers deterministic TTL to avoid noisy eviction at scale.
05:50 Miguel: Console supports TTL-first eviction with probabilistic early evict for very large caches. For your expected 1.2M active session foot print, TTL of 15 minutes with 10% probability early-evict yields stable memory and hit-rate. We'll attach the projected hit-rate vs TTL chart.
06:10 Marcus: Good. Next — batching. You mentioned batch size 64 increased throughput but could increase latency for rare requests. How does concurrency cap interact with batch size?
06:19 Miguel: Two knobs: max batch size and max collect-wait (time the runtime waits to fill a batch). If you set batch size high but collect-wait low (e.g., 10ms), you still get throughput but limit added latency. Concurrency cap controls number of in-flight batches; if concurrency is too low you'll saturate GPU and see queueing. Console's recommendation engine suggests target concurrency based on model throughput benchmarks and your p90 sequence length.
06:45 Lena: Can you show the console's suggested settings for our 90th percentile session?
06:49 Miguel: (selects profile) For your 90p session length ~420 tokens, console suggests max batch 48, collect-wait 12ms, concurrency cap 120 on n1-standard-dedicated (m60). That yields our best throughput/cost sweet spot in the sim.
07:06 Aisha: We also surfaced a 'VIP route' option: you can tag certain sessions to bypass prefetch and use a lower-latency route (different model variant or higher priority pool).
07:16 Priya: That might be handy for account managers. If they need lower latency we'll bypass prefetch and keep small batches.
07:23 Lena: On security: we'll need SOC 2 docs, SAML SSO integration, and KMS for keying. Can you send those?
07:30 Aisha: Yes, we'll share SOC 2 and SAML integration guide after the call. For KMS we support AWS KMS and customer HSM through our Private deployment; we'll note options in the doc.
07:42 Miguel: Back to numbers — I'm going to show the per-route cost table. (shares) Baseline monthly estimate for your projected 200M tokens: $10.6k. With prefetch + batching recommended config: $6.2k — about 42% savings. That's including prefetch tokens and background pool cost.
08:05 Marcus: How sensitive is that to hit-rate? If our hit-rate is 60% instead of 75% for long sessions, what's delta?
08:14 Miguel: The simulator has a slider. Dropping hit-rate to 60% reduces savings to ~28% net. That means prefetch policy needs tuning or you'll want a selective prefetch only for sessions with high prefix reuse.
08:28 Lena: We do have some sessions with highly repetitive prefixes (account-status queries). Can console detect repetitive prefixes automatically?
08:34 Miguel: Yes, Optimize can run a prefix frequency analysis and tag the top N prefixes for deterministic prefetch. It surfaces a list and a recommendation score. We can demo that in the pilot.
08:46 Aisha: Quick interjection — on billing clarity: we'll provide a breakdown of managed compute vs prefetch background compute vs network egress in the spreadsheet.
08:54 Priya: That helps procurement.
08:57 Miguel: Now, an example of a risky config: enable prefetch on same pool, big batch size 128, and high collect-wait. In a spike we see short session 95p to 400+ms and prefetch backlog causes memory pressure. Console flags it as 'dangerous' and recommends falling back to a smaller batch size or moving prefetch off-pool.
09:21 Lena: Ok can you show how rollout would look? We don't want to flip prefetch on all at once.
09:26 Miguel: Rollouts are first-class in the Console: canary by user-segment or by percent of sessions, with automatic rollback if latency SLO breaches or quality regressions detected by your eval set. We'll create a canary for 10% of sessions (non-VIP) route those to the prefetch-enabled pool for two days, monitor 95p latency and token-cost deltas. If both are in target we'll proceed to 30% then 100%.
09:48 Priya: What telemetry do we need to provide?
09:52 Miguel: For the pilot we need a 7-day traffic dump and an eval prompt set for quality regression checks (we'll show how to connect your eval repo). The console ships a dashboard with per-route cost, token delta, latency distribution and a 'quality drift' signal if logits/outputs deviate on your eval set.
10:13 Marcus: About network: if we run Dedicated in our VPC do we still see console metrics?
10:18 Aisha: The Private/Dedicated control plane sends anonymized metrics to Redwood console; sensitive traces can be scrubbed. For fully airgapped on-prem we have an optional telemetry forwarder that pushes only aggregated counters — we'll include that option in the security pack.
10:34 Miguel: Small demo bit — prefix analysis result for GrandBay: top 20 prefixes account for 18% of token volume and have an avg reuse length of 42 tokens. Console suggests priming those prefixes for a 24-hour TTL window; that yields a 14% hit-rate uplift in the sim.
10:55 Lena: Nice. So combining targeted prefix priming + general lookahead prefetch seems better than a broad prefetch.
11:03 Miguel: Exactly — targeted prefix priming reduces background token spend because you're only warming hot prefixes. For long-tail prefixes you can keep lookahead prefetch with a lower horizon.
11:12 Priya: On cost modeling — will you give us the raw assumptions so our finance team can validate? We need per-GPU-hour and per-token compute assumptionsand any margin the managed layer adds.
11:22 Aisha: We'll send the cost model CSV; it includes GPU cost, managed overhead, storage for KV, and a conservative buffer. We can also run a cost-neutral estimate that strips out managed overhead for internal comparison.
11:33 Lena: One more technical: what about model checkpoint variants? If we route to a quantized variant for non-VIP sessions, do you see quality drift?
11:42 Miguel: Console can simulate model-variant routing and shows expected quality delta using your eval set. Often quantized variants hold up well for mid-length sessions but degrade on very long context completions. That's why a hybrid route (quantized + prefetching for long contexts) can be a big win.
12:00 Priya: That hybrid idea is appealing.
12:03 Miguel: Okay final section — pilot plan proposal: 1) GrandBay provides 7-day traffic dump and eval set; 2) Redwood configures a canary (10%) with targeted prefix priming + lookahead 32 tokens on background pool; 3) Run 14-day pilot with daily reports and a final delta table. Success criteria: >=30% net cost reduction for non-VIP segment and 95p <= 220ms for VIPs.
12:30 Lena: That seems reasonable. Timeline?
12:33 Aisha: If we get the traffic dump by Monday, Miguel can run sims within 48 hours and we can schedule the pilot start for the following week.
12:40 Marcus: We'll aim to upload the dump Monday morning.
12:44 Aisha: Great. Any other Qs?
12:46 Priya: Procurement will ask about contract length and reserved capacity. Do you offer a short reserved pilot rate for Dedicated?
12:52 Aisha: Yes we have a 30-day pilot reserved commit with prorated pricing and an option to convert to a 12-month contract. I'll include the pricing cadence in the follow-up.
13:03 Miguel: Small note on observability — console will produce a per-token trace sample and per-request KV-hit header so you can instrument downstream services with KV-hit=%. That helps tie saved token costs to user journeys.
13:20 Lena: Perfect.
13:23 (brief cross-talk about scheduling)
13:28 Aisha: Recap / next steps: I'll send the cost-simulator CSV, SOC 2 + SAML docs, and a proposed pilot SOW. Miguel will run the 3k-sample sim and share logs. GrandBay to upload 7-day traffic dump. We'll reconvene after Miguel's sim to finalize rollout targets.
13:48 Marcus: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
13:50 Aisha: Thanks all.
13:52 End of call.
